title: I missed Empire Earth, so I spent my weekend building a browser RTS that goes from the Stone Age to the future (alpha trailer)
author: bchuckg
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I'm a big RTS fan. Age of Empires has me well covered, but I've always missed a real Empire Earth alternative: more ages, longer eras, and ideally all the way into the future. I also wanted something I can actually play on my Mac.

So I spent my free time this weekend building one. It's called **The Long Empire**, and I've been enjoying playing it myself.

**It's a browser game.** It runs straight in your browser, so there's nothing to install, and it works on Mac, Windows and Linux.

What's in it right now (alpha):

* 6 ages: Stone Age, Bronze Age, Iron Age, Middle Ages, Renaissance, Industrial Age
* Economy in the style of AoE II: villagers gathering food, wood, stone and gold; farms, markets, techs
* AI opponents: four difficulty levels, each with its own personality (rush, boom, turtle…)
* Wars on land and sea: siege, castles, firearms, ships and wonders as a victory condition
* Voxel art style: every unit and building looks different in each age

Planned (coming soon):

* VII World Wars: oil and air power
* VIII Modern Age: the power grid
* IX Digital Age: autonomous drones
* X Future: energy weapons and shields

To be clear, this is an alpha. There are still bugs, especially in pathfinding, and the balancing still needs work.

I had AI put the trailer together quickly. Everything you see in it is real in-game footage from AI-vs-AI matches.

Some questions for you:

* Would you be interested in a game like this?
* Do you think it's worth releasing publicly?

comments.author: DesignerChef5107
comments.body:
Mate, demos like these are impressive but an honest take is that in the end it’s about the whole product. Nobody can truly know from this video alone which in itself does not show proper combat feel or the overall vision. A lot of videos and games are generated nowadays in exceptional quality and this is one among many that look great but in the end it requires playtesting, tons of iteration after feedback and most likely months if not years of testing. Even though we have execution pretty nailed down with AI, taste and feel are not necessarily the same.

To answer your questions, I think most people would be interested in a game like this, yes, but it entirely depends on the execution and cannot really be judged by a one-minute AI video mostly showcasing the art. If this is truly a full-fledged game then of course you should release it publicly but I doubt that is the case here considering it will most likely need way more iteration unless you literally executed the perfect prompts over a weekend.

Also with multiplayer, add some more time on top of that as well. Networking even with AI can be hell.

Good luck with the game!

replies.author: bchuckg
replies.body: Fair point, and I agree: a video can't show feel. It's further along than a weekend: six eras, AI opponents at four difficulty levels, naval combat, saves and replays. But balance and feel need real playtesters, which is exactly why I'm posting. Multiplayer isn't in yet. The sim is deterministic (integer-only, command stream, checksums) so lockstep networking is planned, but I won't promise it before it works.
